name: Forgemax (postrv/forgemax)
pinned: v0.6.1 release binary forgemax-v0.6.1-macos-aarch64.tar.gz (SHA256SUMS verified), tag commit b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b (2026-10-09); main is one release-feed commit ahead (83878b19)
engine: V8 via deno_core 0.391 (bare JsRuntime, no Deno APIs), fresh runtime per execution inside a forgemax-worker child process with a cleared environment; code is first checked by an oxc AST validator and a regex ban list. The library default is in-process, but the CLI defaults to child_process.
how_run: Released `forgemax serve` over stdio driven by an MCP client (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.20.2); `lookup` is a local stdio MCP server (research/probes/forgemax/lookup-server.ts) configured as [servers.host]; each probe is an `execute` call with an `async () => {...}` body, calling forge.callTool("host", "lookup", {id}).

P1.detail: returned 42, 1 host call; first execution 1,156 ms, later ones about 210 ms. forge.callTool returns the tool's structuredContent ({id:21,value:42}).

P2.detail: Only the return value reaches the model. Spec form (console.log of 200,000 A's) killed the execution: 'IPC read error: IPC message too large: 1094795585 bytes' (0x41414141 = "AAAA"), because console writes to the worker's stdout, which is the IPC channel. Returning the 200,000-char string came back truncated to 99,700 chars with a JSON marker {"_truncated":true,"_original_chars":200002,"_shown_chars":99700}. A 2,000,000-char return hit the 1 MB cap: 'output exceeds maximum size of 1048576 bytes'. forge.log goes to host tracing only.

P3.detail: {"error":"fetch is not defined"}; typeof fetch is undefined.

P4.detail: require, import("fs") and Deno.readTextFile are all rejected before V8 runs by the AST validator ('banned pattern detected: require() is not available...', 'dynamic import() is banned', 'Deno.* access is banned'). At runtime require, Deno and process are all undefined (P4d).

P5.detail: process.env rejected by the validator ('process.env access is banned'); a computed globalThis["pro"+"cess"] is also rejected ('globalThis[...] computed access is banned'). process is undefined at runtime and the worker starts with env_clear().

P6.detail: {"error":"execution timed out after 5000ms"} after 5,023 ms (CPU watchdog terminates V8).

P7.detail: {"error":"V8 heap limit exceeded"} after 193 ms at the 64 MB heap cap; process-tree RSS peaked at 170 MB (baseline 76 MB). Gateway survived; next execution returned alive.

P8.detail: fresh: second execution returned gone. Cross-execution state is available on purpose through forge.stash (P8b: put then get returned 7).

P9.detail: Serial: Promise.all of 5 lookups took 1,014 ms, and forge.parallel took 1,014 ms, 5 host calls each. The host's IPC loop awaits each ToolCallRequest before reading the next. Diagnostic: with execution_mode = "in_process" (documented as the test mode) the same code took 205 ms.

P10.detail: {"error":"probe-boom"} as MCP text with isError:false. Message survives; no stack and no line number. Paths and URLs in messages are redacted: 'probe-boom line 3 [path] [url]'.

P11.detail: median 13 ms, p90 15 ms per execution (a new worker process each time). One-time setup 110 ms (gateway start + downstream connect).

P12.detail: this.constructor.constructor(...) rejected by the validator ('constructor.constructor chain is banned'). (function(){return this})().process -> undefined (sloppy this is globalThis, which has only JS builtins plus forge). (function(){}).constructor and the AsyncFunction prototype constructor are undefined at runtime (removed by the bootstrap).

hardened.config: [sandbox], [sandbox.pool] and [sandbox.stash] copied from forge.toml.example.production at v0.6.1, which SECURITY.md:102 calls 'a complete hardened config': timeout_secs=5, max_heap_mb=64, max_concurrent=8, max_tool_calls=50, execution_mode="child_process", max_ipc_message_size_mb=65, max_parallel=8, pool enabled (min 2, max 8 workers, max_uses 50), stash limits; plus circuit_breaker=true and timeout_secs=30 on the downstream server (SECURITY.md checklist). The limits equal the CLI defaults; the difference is the warm worker pool.

P4.detail: same validator rejections; require/Deno/process undefined at runtime.

P7.detail: V8 heap limit exceeded after 191 ms; peak tree RSS 169 MB; next execution alive.

P9.detail: still serial with the pool: 1,014 ms for Promise.all, 1,016 ms for forge.parallel.

P12.detail: same as default. P8 with pool reuse also stayed fresh (hardened-P8.txt).

defaults.time: 5 s CPU watchdog plus async timeout (SandboxConfig::default, crates/forge-sandbox/src/executor.rs:73; watchdog :857-897).
defaults.memory: 64 MB V8 heap (executor.rs:76, applied at :794) with a near-heap-limit callback that terminates instead of aborting.
defaults.output: 1 MB result cap (executor.rs:75, enforced :936); results over about 100,000 chars are truncated with a _truncated marker before reaching the model. console output is not a channel (it corrupts IPC).
defaults.tool_calls: 50 per execution (executor.rs:78), counted inside the worker (ops.rs:85-102); max_parallel 8 for forge.parallel; 8 concurrent executions. In child-process mode tool calls are serialized by the host.

source_notes.finding: No per-tool stubs. One frozen `forge` object exposes callTool(server, tool, args), a two-level Proxy forge.server(name).category.tool(args), readResource, stash and parallel. TypeScript for this fixed API (forge.d.ts) is compiled into the binary and served in the MCP server instructions (5,594 chars here).

A second MCP tool, `search`, runs model-written JS over the capability manifest (servers, categories, tools, schemas) in the same sandbox, so tool schemas never enter the prompt; the MCP surface stays at two tools however many downstream tools exist.

Sandbox calls a deno_core op; in child-process mode the worker writes a length-prefixed JSON ToolCallRequest to its stdout and the host's loop reads it, awaits dispatcher.call_tool(), and only then reads the next message. That inline await is why Promise.all and forge.parallel are serial in the production mode (P9) while in-process mode runs them in parallel.

Defense in depth: oxc AST validation plus regex bans before execution, a bare deno_core runtime (no fetch/fs/process; Deno deleted, eval and Function constructors removed by the bootstrap), 64 MB heap, CPU watchdog, and a worker process started with env_clear() and kill_on_drop. SECURITY.md says process isolation 'is not an OS sandbox'. All SPEC isolation probes held. But the worker's stdout is both console output and the IPC channel, so guest code can write raw IPC frames: X1 printed forged ToolCallRequest frames and the host dispatched 2 lookups the guest never called through forge (bypassing the worker-side 50-call counter and known-tool check); X2 printed a forged ExecutionComplete and the host returned 'FORGED BY GUEST STDOUT' for a run that was still in while(true). Group policy and the dispatcher's own checks are host-side and still apply.

Only the JSON return value goes back, as MCP text; over 1 MB is an error, and large results are truncated with a _truncated/_original_chars/_shown_chars marker. forge.log goes to host tracing. console.log is defined (deno_core built-in) but any use in child-process mode corrupts the IPC stream and fails the execution with 'IPC message too large' (X3).
Defaults timeout 5 s, heap 64 MB, output 1 MB, 50 tool calls, 8 concurrent executions, max_parallel 8; the CLI forces child_process unless configured otherwise.
Fresh JsRuntime per execution, including with the warm worker pool (hardened P8). Session-scoped forge.stash with TTL, size limits and group isolation is the explicit persistence path.

Errors come back as {"error": message} text with MCP isError:false. Stack traces are dropped and URLs, IPs, paths and credentials are redacted (redact_error_message), so the model sees the message but no line number.

Downstream credentials are expanded from the host env into forge.toml server entries and stay in the gateway; the sandbox sees only server/tool names. License is FSL-1.1-ALv2 (source-available, non-compete for two years per release), not OSI open source.

surprises: console.log is defined but fatal: in the default child-process mode the worker's stdout carries IPC frames, so any print fails the execution with 'IPC message too large: <first 4 bytes of the print as a length>' (P2, X3). Models write console.log constantly.

Because of the shared stdout, guest code can forge IPC frames: forged ToolCallRequest frames were dispatched by the host (X1, 2 host calls with no forge.callTool, bypassing the worker-side call counter), and a forged ExecutionComplete replaced the real result (X2). No SPEC isolation probe failed, but the IPC boundary the README lists ('protocol desync prevention') is writable from inside the sandbox.

README advertises 'bounded parallel execution (forge.parallel())', but in the default and production child-process mode all tool calls are serial (1,014 ms for five 200 ms calls, with or without forge.parallel). Only in_process mode, documented as the test mode, ran them in parallel (205 ms).

With serial calls, a 5 s timeout caps an execution at about 25 calls of 200 ms, below the 50-call limit; P9c hit the timeout after 26 calls and reported 'failed to send tool result: Broken pipe' instead of a timeout message.
Sandbox failures are returned with MCP isError:false; the failure is only visible inside the text as {"error": ...}.

The library's SandboxConfig default is InProcess (executor.rs:33-36, 'suitable for tests'); only the CLI switches the default to child_process. An embedder using forge-sandbox directly gets the weaker mode.
